sources.title: NASA Glenn Research Center · Turbofan engine

parts.name: Spinner (nose cone)
parts.purpose: Smooths air into the fan and sheds ice and debris away from the blade roots.
parts.connection: Bolted to the front of the fan hub; turns with the fan and the low-pressure spool.

parts.name: Fan
parts.purpose: The big front rotor. In a high-bypass engine most of the thrust comes from air the fan pushes around the core, not through it.
parts.connection: Driven by the low-pressure turbine through the low-pressure shaft. Its air splits: most goes down the bypass duct, some into the core.
parts.model_note: 22 blades shown; real counts vary by engine.

parts.name: Fan containment case
parts.purpose: A strong ring around the fan that would contain a released blade.
parts.connection: Mounted inside the nacelle, close around the fan-blade tips; that tight gap keeps the fan efficient.

parts.name: Nacelle (engine cowling)
parts.purpose: The aerodynamic outer cowling: it shapes the inlet, lines the bypass duct and forms the fan nozzle at the back.
parts.connection: Surrounds the fan case and bypass duct; in service it hinges open for maintenance and carries the thrust reverser.
parts.model_note: Cut away so the fan and core stay visible.

parts.name: Outlet guide vanes
parts.purpose: Stationary vanes behind the fan that straighten the swirling bypass air so it produces thrust instead of spin.
parts.connection: Span the bypass duct between the core cowl and the outer duct wall, just downstream of the fan.

parts.name: Core cowl & splitter
parts.purpose: The smooth inner wall of the bypass duct. Its sharp front edge, the splitter, divides fan air between bypass and core.
parts.connection: Wraps the whole core, from just behind the fan to the core nozzle.
parts.model_note: Cut away so the core stays visible.

parts.name: Low-pressure compressor (booster)
parts.purpose: The booster: a few stages that begin squeezing the air entering the core.
parts.connection: On the low-pressure spool with the fan, so it turns at fan speed.

parts.name: High-pressure compressor
parts.purpose: Many stages of small blades that squeeze the core air to a small fraction of its volume before it burns.
parts.connection: On the high-pressure spool, driven by the high-pressure turbine at a much higher speed than the fan.

parts.name: Compressor casing & stator vanes
parts.purpose: Holds the stationary stator vanes between the rotating compressor stages; each stator row turns the flow to feed the next rotor.
parts.connection: Encloses both compressors and ties the fan frame to the combustor casing.
parts.model_note: Cut away; stator rows shown between rotor stages.

parts.name: Combustion chamber (annular)
parts.purpose: The ring-shaped chamber where fuel burns continuously in the compressed air, raising its temperature enormously.
parts.connection: Takes air from the high-pressure compressor and feeds the hot gas straight into the high-pressure turbine.

parts.name: Fuel nozzles & manifold
parts.purpose: Spray finely atomised fuel into the combustor so it mixes and burns quickly and evenly.
parts.connection: A fuel manifold ring feeds each nozzle through the combustor casing.

parts.name: Combustor & turbine casing
parts.purpose: The pressure vessel around the combustor and turbines.
parts.connection: Bolts to the compressor casing in front and carries the turbine vanes and exhaust hardware.
parts.model_note: Cut away so the combustor and turbines are visible.

parts.name: High-pressure turbine
parts.purpose: The first turbine: extracts energy from the hottest gas to drive the high-pressure compressor. Its blades are internally cooled.
parts.connection: Directly behind the combustor, joined to the high-pressure compressor by the high-pressure shaft.

parts.name: Turbine nozzle guide vanes
parts.purpose: Stationary vanes that accelerate and aim the hot gas onto each row of turbine blades.
parts.connection: Alternate with the rotating turbine stages, held by the turbine casing.

parts.name: Low-pressure turbine
parts.purpose: Several stages that take the remaining energy from the gas to drive the fan and booster.
parts.connection: Behind the high-pressure turbine; joined to the fan by the low-pressure shaft running through the middle of the engine.

parts.name: Core exhaust nozzle
parts.purpose: Accelerates the core exhaust rearward for the last part of the thrust.
parts.connection: At the end of the core, inside the fan stream.

parts.name: Exhaust plug (tail cone)
parts.purpose: Shapes the core exhaust as it leaves the engine.
parts.connection: Fixed to the turbine exhaust frame at the centre of the core nozzle.

parts.name: Low-pressure shaft
parts.purpose: The inner shaft: carries power from the low-pressure turbine forward to the fan.
parts.connection: Runs inside the hollow high-pressure shaft; the two spools turn independently at different speeds.

parts.name: High-pressure shaft
parts.purpose: The outer, hollow shaft joining the high-pressure turbine to the high-pressure compressor.
parts.connection: Concentric around the low-pressure shaft.

parts.name: Accessory gearbox & tower shaft
parts.purpose: Drives the fuel pump, oil pump and generators, and receives the starter to spin the engine up.
parts.connection: A tower shaft takes power off the high-pressure spool down to the gearbox.
